takeaway: Secretin does not stimulate gastrin release (the exception). Vagus drives the cephalic phase, most secretion is in the gastric phase, somatostatin inhibits gastrin, fat releases CCK.

question.text: Regarding the regulation of gastric secretion, the following statements are true except:

answer.text: Secretin from the duodenum stimulating gastrin release is the false statement.

lines.text: Here the false statement is secretin stimulating gastrin release.
Gastric secretion has three phases. First, the cephalic phase: the sight or smell of food, and vagal activity stimulates secretion.
The vagus also stimulates G-cells to release gastrin, which drives more acid.
Most secretion happens in the gastric phase, once food reaches the stomach.
Fatty food in the duodenum releases cholecystokinin.
Somatostatin is the brake: it inhibits gastrin secretion.
But secretin does not stimulate gastrin, so that is the exception.
